title: SQL Data Types
description: SQL data types define the kind of data that can be stored in a table column. Choosing the correct data type is essential for data integrity and performance.

points: SMALLINT – Stores smaller range of integers
DECIMAL(p, s) – Stores exact numeric values with precision
DOUBLE PRECISION – Stores high-precision floating-point numbers
TIMESTAMP – Stores date and time together
BOOLEAN – Stores TRUE or FALSE values
JSONB – Stores binary JSON (optimized for querying)

content.description: Constraints are rules applied to table columns to enforce data integrity.
types: PRIMARY KEY – Uniquely identifies each row

complete_example.heading: Complete Example Using Multiple Data Types

create_table.query:
CREATE TABLE employees (
  emp_id SERIAL PRIMARY KEY,
  full_name VARCHAR(100) NOT NULL,
  age INT,
  salary DECIMAL(10,2),
  is_active BOOLEAN DEFAULT true,
  joining_date DATE,
  created_at TIMESTAMP DEFAULT CURRENT_TIMESTAMP
);

insert_data.query:
INSERT INTO employees (full_name, age, salary, is_active, joining_date)
